original_question: For each integer h > 1, determine the smallest number of vertices that a graph can have while having obstacle number exactly h.
target_in_paper: Section 2.5, Open Problem 10: "For h > 1, what is the smallest number of vertices of a graph with obstacle number h?" ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the official problem almost verbatim: it quantifies over integers h>1, asks for the minimum possible number of vertices, and requires obstacle number exactly h, which is exactly the content of Open Problem 10. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
missing_details: The draft is not fully stand-alone because the paper defines obstacle number through an obstacle representation in the plane: graph vertices are represented by points and obstacles are simple polygons. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

The adjacency rule should be stated explicitly: two vertices are adjacent exactly when the straight-line segment between their representative points does not intersect any obstacle. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

The paper imposes a general-position assumption: the segment joining any two representative points does not pass through another representative point or through a vertex of an obstacle. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

To stay paper-faithful, the minimization should be understood in this polygonal-obstacle model in the Euclidean plane, not in convex-obstacle, grid-obstacle, or other variant models. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

The nearby context records that for every positive integer h there exists a graph with obstacle number exactly h, which explains why asking for the smallest possible order for fixed h is meaningful. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
refined_question: For each integer h>1, determine the minimum number of vertices of a finite graph G with obstacle number obs(G)=h, where obs(G) denotes the minimum number of simple polygonal obstacles in a plane obstacle representation of G: the vertices of G are represented by points in the plane, two vertices are adjacent if and only if the segment joining their representative points avoids every obstacle, and all representative points and obstacle vertices are assumed to be in general position so that no such segment passes through another representative point or an obstacle vertex. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
justification: This draft clearly targets Section 2.5, Open Problem 10 rather than the neighboring Open Problems 8 and 9: it fixes h and asks for the smallest order of a graph whose obstacle number is exactly h, whereas Open Problems 8 and 9 ask for upper and lower bounds on obstacle number as a function of n. The only substantive additions needed are the model assumptions given immediately before Open Problem 10—namely, the plane obstacle-representation definition, the use of simple polygonal obstacles, and the general-position convention. I therefore kept the question as narrow as the paper does and only made those hidden assumptions explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
